topic: Data Preprocessing: Handling Outliers, Missing Values, and Skewed Data

questions.scenario: Real-world Industrial Problem Statement: A Tier-1 fintech core-banking platform monitors transactions across 180 continuous telemetry features to detect fraudulent wire transfers in real time. The event stream processes roughly 40,000 transactions per second with strict P99 latency bounds of under 12 milliseconds. Initial deployment utilized Mahalanobis Distance for multivariate outlier detection; however, the model pipeline suffered from covariance matrix instability due to high multicollinearity, alongside computational bottlenecks ($O(d^3)$ inversion overhead per batch update).
questions.question: Which algorithm and configuration strategy should the data engineering team adopt to isolate multivariate outliers effectively under these high-dimensional and sub-second execution constraints?
options: A) Local Outlier Factor (LOF) using k-d trees with Minkowski $p=3$ distance metric.
B) Minimum Covariance Determinant (MCD) leveraging FastMCD approximation with full rank validation.
C) Isolation Forest with subsampling size constrained to $\psi=256$ and path-length estimation across an ensemble of randomized trees.
D) DBSCAN with parameter tuning through k-distance graphs utilizing exact pairwise Euclidean distance computation.
questions.correct_answer_text: C) Isolation Forest with subsampling size constrained to $\psi=256$ and path-length estimation across an ensemble of randomized trees.
questions.explanation: Isolation Forest exhibits an average-case time complexity of $O(t \cdot \psi \log \psi)$, where $t$ is the number of trees and $\psi$ is the sub-sampling size. A small subsample (e.g., 256) circumvents masking and swamping effects while mitigating the curse of dimensionality that plagues distance-based methods like LOF and DBSCAN ($O(N^2)$ or $O(N \log N)$). Furthermore, Isolation Forest does not require computing matrix inverses or calculating expensive pairwise metrics, making it uniquely suitable for high-throughput streaming pipelines within tight millisecond SLAs.

questions.scenario: Real-world Industrial Problem Statement: An intensive care unit (ICU) clinical decision support system predicts 48-hour patient sepsis onset. Several continuous biomarkers (such as serum lactate, arterial blood gas, and C-reactive protein) exhibit 45% missingness. Exploratory analysis reveals the data is Missing Not at Random (MNAR): clinicians order these specific panels primarily when a patient displays symptomatic deterioration. Complete Case Analysis (listwise deletion) removes 70% of the patient cohort and introduces severe selection bias, while standard mean or median imputation distorts the feature variance and eliminates the clinical signal inherent in the missingness.
questions.question: Which imputation and feature engineering methodology is statistically optimal to preserve the predictive capacity of the downstream gradient boosted decision trees without introducing data leakage?
options: A) K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) imputation computed over the entire unified dataset prior to k-fold cross-validation partitioning.
B) Multivariate Imputation by Chained Equations (MICE) paired with missingness indicator vectors (MissingIndicator), fitted strictly on the training partition.
C) Forward-fill (LOCF) across all patient records globally, backed by constant replacement with global maximum feature limits.
D) Listwise deletion augmented with Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE) to synthetically balance mortality labels.
questions.correct_answer_text: B) Multivariate Imputation by Chained Equations (MICE) paired with missingness indicator vectors (MissingIndicator), fitted strictly on the training partition.
questions.explanation: When data is Missing Not at Random (MNAR), the fact that a measurement is missing contains informative predictive value. Augmenting the feature space with binary missingness indicators (MissingIndicator) explicitly exposes this non-random clinical intent to the tree models. Using Multivariate Imputation by Chained Equations (MICE) models each feature conditional on the others, preserving multivariable dependencies and uncertainty far better than single-value imputation. Crucially, fitting the imputation estimators exclusively on the training split prevents data leakage into the validation/testing folds.

questions.scenario: Real-world Industrial Problem Statement: An enterprise retail analytics engine models Customer Lifetime Value (CLV) to optimize bidding across programmatic ad auctions. The target variable (365-day net realized spend) features high zero-inflation (82% of users spend exactly $0) and an extreme, heavy right-tail Pareto distribution (kurtosis > 45, skewness > 8.5) among spending users. The machine learning pipeline relies on an ElasticNet-regularized Generalized Linear Model (GLM). Applying standard Box-Cox transformation fails because the feature domain contains non-positive values ($y = 0$). Adding an arbitrary uniform shift ($y + c$) severely biases the log-likelihood optimization.
questions.question: Which mathematical transformation should be deployed to normalize the target distribution and stabilize residual variance across the entire non-negative real domain without arbitrary shifting?
options: A) Yeo-Johnson Power Transformation optimized via Maximum Likelihood Estimation across the parameter $\lambda$.
B) Standard Min-Max Normalization scaled to the range $[-1, 1]$.
C) Z-score standardization followed by quantile trimming at the 99th percentile.
D) Continuous Logarithmic Transform with zero-replacement using the empirical mean of non-zero values.
questions.correct_answer_text: A) Yeo-Johnson Power Transformation optimized via Maximum Likelihood Estimation across the parameter $\lambda$.
questions.explanation: The Yeo-Johnson transformation extends the Box-Cox framework to support zero and negative values continuously. Its piecewise formulation for non-negative values ($y \ge 0$) with $\lambda \ne 0$ is defined as $((y + 1)^\lambda - 1) / \lambda$, and $\log(y + 1)$ when $\lambda = 0$. By optimizing the parameter $\lambda$ using Maximum Likelihood Estimation (MLE), it dampens extreme right skewness and handles the massive zero mass natively without introducing an arbitrary, empirically ungrounded hyperparameter shift ($c$). Min-Max and Z-score transformations are linear mappings that preserve skewness rather than resolving it.
